questions.q: Which tool do you use to change the report server's service account or set up scale-out?
options: Report Server Configuration Manager
The web portal's Site Settings page
SQL Server Management Studio's Security folder
Report Builder's Options dialog
questions.explain: The Configuration Manager is the machine-level tool for the service account, URLs, database, scale-out, and email delivery — settings the web portal can't touch.

questions.q: Where would a content manager go to add a system-level role assignment without touching the server machine?
options: The web portal's Site Settings > Security page
Report Server Configuration Manager's Service Account tab
The RDL file's XML directly
Windows Server's Local Users and Groups console
questions.explain: System-level role assignments are configured entirely in the browser, on Site Settings > Security in the web portal.

options: Multiple report server instances that share one report server database
A report that runs across multiple SQL Server instances at once
A subscription that delivers to multiple email addresses
A dataset that queries multiple data sources simultaneously
questions.explain: Scale-out lets several report server instances point at the same shared database — configured per-instance through Configuration Manager.

questions.q: What does the symmetric key protect, and why does it matter for administration?
options: It encrypts stored connection strings and credentials, so you need a backup before moving the database or changing the service account
It signs RDL files so Report Builder can validate authorship
It encrypts the report cache so users can't read cached copies directly
It's used only for HTTPS certificate validation on the web portal
questions.explain: The symmetric key encrypts stored connection strings and credentials — without a backup, changing the service account or moving the database can strand encrypted data.

questions.q: Which tabs live on the web portal's Site Settings page?
options: General, Security, and Schedules
Service Account, URLs, and Database
Datasets, Data Sources, and Subscriptions
Report History, Parameters, and Caching
questions.explain: Site Settings covers General (site-wide defaults), Security (system-level roles), and Schedules (shared schedules) — the day-to-day admin knobs, not machine-level setup.
